stories.headline: Steve Visits the Eastern Ridge; Mrs. Holt Explains the Hats; the Explanation Is Not What Anyone Expected
body: Steve Fairweather made his third visit to the eastern ridge on Monday morning, hat log in hand, with the stated intention of thanking Mrs. Elspeth Holt for the deerstalker and the unstated intention of asking about it. He was offered tea before he reached the gate.

Mrs. Holt, 81, confirmed over the course of one pot and most of a second that she began hatting ducks in 1987. The cause was not sentiment, nor craft, nor a desire to mystify Jeep owners thirty years hence. 'Bare ducks look cold,' she said. 'That's the whole of it.' She added that she had made one exception, once, for a mallard that had asked for a beret and been refused on grounds of character.

Steve has recorded this in the hat log under the heading 'Foundational Principles.' He also noted that Mrs. Holt paused, near the end of the second pot, and mentioned that her late husband had driven these ridges — 'same hollows, before the mud got worse' — and that she had started leaving things on other people's vehicles after that, 'just to be friendly.' The hat log entry for this observation is brief. Steve wrote: 'See also: why we go.' Five ducks remain.

serial.title: The Six Remaining Ducks of Elspeth Holt

stories.headline: Monday Queue Proceeds in Order; One Account-Holder Arrives Uncertain of His Question; Christine Identifies the Question; Question Answered; Account-Holder Departs Knowing What He Came For
body: Monday's full ledger at Gringotts was cleared by mid-afternoon without material incident, a result attributed by floor staff to 'the usual reasons,' the usual reasons being Christine.

One account-holder, a Mr. Pemberton of Clegg's Cross, arrived at the liaison window unable to articulate his concern but certain he had one. Christine listened for approximately forty seconds, asked two questions, and identified the concern as a minor compound-interest discrepancy dating to March. Mr. Pemberton confirmed this was indeed the concern and expressed some surprise that he had not known it himself. The discrepancy was resolved. Mr. Pemberton left with the expression of a man who has found his keys in his own pocket.

stories.headline: The Kitchen Shelf Receives a Formal Inspection; Shelf Passes; Don's Portrait Requests the Record Reflect That He Would Have Used a Different Bracket
body: The newly installed kitchen shelf — cleared last week for up to eight items after a controlled load trial — received an informal structural review on Monday, conducted by Steve and observed by Don's portrait, whose commentary was offered at no charge.

The shelf passed. It is level. The fixings are sound. Steve confirmed all points with a spirit level and received no argument from the wall. Don's portrait acknowledged the craftsmanship, paused, and noted that he personally would have countersunk the bracket screws and used a slightly wider span, 'but it'll hold.' Steve thanked him. The portrait looked satisfied in the manner of someone who has made their point without escalating it. The shelf continues to hold eight items. A ninth has not been proposed.

stories.headline: Ellie Investigates a Sound; Sound Is the Refrigerator; Investigation Ongoing
body: Ellie, familiar of the household, spent a portion of Monday afternoon stationed six inches from the kitchen refrigerator, ears forward, monitoring what she has described through available means as 'an ongoing and unresolved hum.' The refrigerator's compressor cycle has operated on an unchanged schedule since installation.
Ellie has not resolved the investigation. She has, however, established a perimeter. Jersey observed from the settee. Lucy did not look up.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Reviewed the hat log while Steve was out. Made two annotations. Has replaced them with blank space. The log reads more cleanly now.
Ellie: The hum is still there. She is still there. One of them will blink first. Ellie's record on this front is mixed but her commitment is not.
Jersey: Monday is, in Jersey's considered view, one of the better days for lap-sitting — the light is low, the blanket is where it should be, and no one has yet asked him to move. He has not moved.
founding_editor_note: I built those presses with a hand level and a good eye and they have never hummed unexpectedly, which is more than I can say for that refrigerator. — D.

in_brief.sport: Gringotts Vault Carry Championship postponed pending quorum; Christine is the quorum.
in_brief.forecast: Light mist through the hollows by evening; five ducks outstanding; conditions described by Steve as 'about right.'

storyline_updates.title: The Six Remaining Ducks of Elspeth Holt
storyline_updates.summary: Day 3: Steve visited the ridge and learned why Mrs. Holt hats ducks — bare ducks look cold, full stop — but also discovered a quieter reason: her late husband drove these same ridges, and she began leaving things on other people's vehicles afterward, 'just to be friendly.' Steve logged it under 'why we go.' Five ducks remain at the ridge, unscheduled. The deerstalker note ('This one is for the detective') is still unresolved; Lucy has not clarified. Day 4 should bring another duck — perhaps hand-delivered again, or with a note that nudges the 'detective' question toward resolution — and may begin to build toward whatever the final duck's arrival will mean: a completion, a small ceremony, or simply Mrs. Holt on the porch with the last hatted duck and nothing more to say but everything said.
